disposition_reason: Tables 2 and 3 print min, max, mean and SD of As, Pb, Cd, Cu and Zn (mg/kg) in maize, rice, millet, sorghum, cowpea, soybean and groundnuts bought at Tamale Aboabo market in December 2017.

study.design: Market survey with health risk assessment
study.origin: not stated (market draws on Northern Region farms and West African imports)
study.market: Tamale Aboabo market, Tamale, Northern Region, Ghana
study.method: HNO3 hot-block digestion of 5 g dried sample; flame AAS (Shimadzu AA 6300) at CSIR-WRI Tamale
lod: As 0.02, Cd 0.04, Zn 0.02, Pb 2.0, Cu 0.3 (units not stated)
study.qa: Triplicate measurements, blanks; recovery 92-103% for calibration standards; no CRM

findings.notes: Three samples per food bought at Tamale Aboabo market, Northern Region, Ghana, December 2017, combined into a composite before grinding; HNO3 digestion; flame AAS (Shimadzu AA 6300). Recoveries 92-103%. Printed LODs (units not stated): As 0.02, Cd 0.04, Zn 0.02, Pb 2.0, Cu 0.3. Basis: dried sample (constant weight). Copper (0.02-0.05 mg/kg) and zinc (0.003-0.09 mg/kg) are roughly 100 to 1000 times below typical grain and legume levels and below their own printed LODs, suggesting a unit or calculation problem across the tables.
